ORDER
In this Order, the Arkansas Public Sendce Commission (Commission) approves
the Settlement Agreement filed August 30, 2019, by Entergy Arkansas, LLC (EAL or the
Company) (formerly Arkansas Power and Light Company) and the General Staff (Staff)
ofthe Commission (collectively, Settling Parties).1
I.
PROCEDURAL HISTORY
On March 29, 2019, EAL filed its Motion for Approval of Revised Estimate of
Arkansas Nuclear One Decommissioning Costs (Motion) with the Commission.
The
Motion provides a revised estimate for decommissioning costs (2019 Estimate) for
Arkansas Nuclear One Unit i and Unit 2 (collectively, ANO), as required by Order No.
61. The 2019 Estimate is approximately $2.007 billion ($1.615 billion excluding post-
shutdown spent fuel management costs). EAL states that the 2019 Estimate, excluding
spent
fuel
management
costs,
is
about
21
percent
more
than
the
previous
decommissioning cost estimate, also excluding post-shutdown spent fuel management
costs.
The Motion recommends discontinuing the evaluation of the ENTOMB
decommissioning alternative for filings beginning in 2024. Motion 1111 1-5. That same
day, EAL filed the Direct Testimony and Exhibits of William A. Cloutier in support of the
2019 Estimate.
1 Arkansas Electric Energy Consumers, Inc. is also a party to the Docket and does not oppose the
Settlement Agreement.

On April 3, 2019, EAL submitted the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC)
Status of Decommissioning Funding Report that it previously had filed with the NRC on
March 28, 2019. On April 8, 2019, Staff filed its Response to EAL's Motion. On April
l8, 2019, Staff submitted a Motion to Establish a Procedural Schedule, which was
subsequently amended on April 25, 2019.
On April 26, 2019, the Commission issued
Order No. 67, which granted the Amended Procedural Schedule.
On July 23, 2019, Staff submitted the Direct Testimony and Exhibits of Dan
Daves.
On August 6, 2019, EAL submitted the Rebuttal Testimony of Francis W.
Seymore. On August 20, 2019, Staff submitted the Surrebuttal Testimony and Exhibit
of Dan Daves.
On August 27, 2019, EAL submitted the Sur-Surrebuttal Testimony of
Francis W. Seymore.
On August 30, 2019, EAL and Staff submitted a Joint Motion to Approve
Settlement and Cancel Hearing (Joint Motion). On September 3, 2019, Staff filed the
Agreement Testimony of Dan Daves, while EAL filed the Settlement Testimony of
Francis W. Seymore. That same day, the Commission issued Order No. 68, granting the
Settling Parties' Joint Motion to cancel the hearing and agreeing to decide the matter on
the existing record.
II.
SUMMARY OF THE PARTIES' POSITIONS BEFORE SETTLEMENT
A.
EAL's Direct Testimonv
EAL witness William A. Cloutier testifies that he is a manager for TLG Ser^ices,
Inc. which has been hired by EAL to prepare the 2019 decommissioning cost estimate.
Mr. Cloutier recites that in Order No. 61, which was filed in this Docket in 2014, EAL
was directed to provide the following information in future five-year cost filings:

"
file in this Docket within thirty days a copy of any NRC filing by EAL or an
afffliate relating to ANO decommissioning;
"
a thorough explanation for any increase greater than the average annual
inflation rate as measured by the CPI-U over the same five-year period;
"
the best available information comparing EAL's cost estimates with actual
decommissioning costs for United States nuclear plants already out of
service;
"
information regarding industry and site-specific factors that may cause
costs to increase greater than the CPI-U;
"
a recommendation, based on the best available information at the time,
whether to discontinue evaluation on the ENTOMB method in filings
beginning in 2024.
Cloutier Direct at 3-4.
Mr. Cloutier states that EAL's 2019 Estimate fully satisfies the requirements set
forth in the NRC's regulations. Mr. Cloutier discusses some of the prior cost estimates
that TLG has prepared for other utilities that have been approved by the NRC.
To
develop the 2019 Estimate, Mr. Cloutier states that TLG used the same methodology
found in two publications:
(i) the AIF/NESP-036 study report "Guidelines for
Producing Commercial Nuclear Power Plant Decommissioning Cost Estimates and (2)
the "Decommissioning Handbook" of the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE).
He
explains that these two publications use a unit cost factor method to estimate costs for
each activity such as concert removal or steel removal. Id. at 5-8.

Mr.
Cloutier
states that
the
NRC
allows
the
cholce
of three
different
decommissioning alternatives: DECON (prompt removal/ dismantling), SAFSTOR
(mothballing), and, under special circumstances,
ENTOMB (entombment).
He
describes each alternative in more detail. He notes that the Commission has directed
EAL to include cost analysis for each of the three alternative methods in its 2019
Estimate and that in 2017 the NRC proposed removing any discussion of the ENTOMB
option from existing guidance documents.
Mr. Cloutier states that the NRC has
determined that the method is not practical or feasible for current U.S. power reactors,
and the timeframe for completing the decommissioning of a plant using the ENTOMB
method is generally inconsistent with current regulations. Id. at 9-10.
Mr.
Cloutier
states
that
TLG
prepared
cost
analyses
for
the
three
decommissioning alternatives.
He states further that the ENTOMB option does not
appear to have merit for ANO, and therefore recommends discontinuing the evaluation
of this method starting in 2024. He points out that no commercial nuclear plant in the
U.S. has attempted an ENTOMB decommissioning method, and regulatory guidance on
the method is limited at best. Id. at 11-12.
Mr. Cloutier explains that the 2019 Estimate not only includes the costs for
removing the contaminated material, but also includes the cost for dismantling the
remaining structures and grading the site. He notes that the largest cost component is
for dismantling the decontaminated structures and the next largest cost is related to
removing certain non-contaminated systems and components.
He testifies that this
work is required before the NRC will issue a license termination and release of the site
for another use. Id. at 13-15.

Mr. Cloutier states that the 2019 Estimate also includes a management plan for
spent fuel storage. Mr. Cloutier notes that the 2019 Estimate does not include costs for
the removal or disposal of spent nuclear fuel because it is ultimately the responsibility of
the DOE.
He explains that the 2019 Estimate does, however, consider the increased
costs associated with delaying certain decommissioning activities related to the spent
fuel area of the plant.
Mr. Cloutier discusses the history behind the DOE's plans for
disposing of the spent fuel. Mr. Cloutier states that the post-operation caretaking costs
ofthe spent fuel totals $13.4 million. Id. at 15-21.
Mr. Cloutier provides the total cost for each ofthe three scenarios:
"
$2.007 billion for DECON
"
$2.231 billion for SAFSTOR
"
$2.262 billion for ENTOMB
Mr. Cloutier states that each estimate includes an uncertainty and risk contingency
factor of 16.9 percent to 17.7 percent.
He testifies that the 2019 DECON estimate of
$2.o07billion is a 19.8 percent increase over the 2014 DECON estimate of $1.676 billion
(in 2014 dollars). Mr. Cloutier states that after considering the CPI-U inflation rate of
14 percent for the five-year period, the increase is $96.6 million. Id. at 21-23.
Mr. Cloutier states that one-third ofthe $96.6 million cost increase is associated
with the longer independent spent fuel storage installation operating period in the 2019
Estimate. Mr. Cloutier testifies that in the 2014 Estimate, TLG assumed that the DOE
would begin removing the spent fuel from the commercial nuclear plants in 2025. Mr.
Cloutier states that with no progress by the DOE over the past five years, TLG changed
the start date to 2030 in the 2019 Estimate.
Mr. Cloutier states that two additional

drivers of the increase in excess of the CPI-U are (i) the need for additional
decommissioning resources that has been shown through current experience with actual
decommissioning projects, and (2) increases in waste processing costs.
Mr. Cloutier
discusses the reasons individual cost items increased at a rate greater than inflation. He
provides a table that compares the 2019 Estimate to actual decommissioning costs
reported to the NRC for plants already out of service. Id. at 23-29.
Mr. Cloutier testifies that the contingency is a provision to account for costs
related to unforeseen problems which will increase costs, and are likely to occur but
cannot be accurately predicted. Mr. Cloutier notes that the Contingency Factor is not a
cushion or safety factor. Instead, he states that the contingency amount is expected to
be spent during the decommissioning process. Id. at 29-31.
Mr.
Cloutier provides
detailed
descriptions
of the three
phases
in the
decommissioning process. He recommends that the decommissioning cost continue to
be funded based upon the DECON alternative.
He states that the 2019 Estimate for
DECON, excluding spent fuel management costs, is $1.615 billion.
Finally, he
recommends that the Commission discontinue the evaluation of the ENTOMB method
in future decommissioning filings. Id. at 32-39.
B.
StafPs Direct Testimonv
Staff witness Daves summarizes the five additional directives in Commission
Order No. 61 filed in this Docket on November 10, 2014.
Mr. Daves states that EAL
complied with all but one ofthe directives. He states that EAL was directed to provide a
thorough explanation for any increase greater than the average annual inflation rate as
APSC FILED Time: 10/9/2019 10:29:55 AM: Recvd 10/9/2019 10:29:50 AM: Docket 87-166-TF-Doc. 335

measured by the CPI-U over the same five year period. He states that EAL did not fully
comply with this directive. Daves Direct at 3-7.
Mr. Daves briefly describes the analysis that he performed.
He states that Mr.
Cloutier's CPI-U inflation increase of 14 percent over the five-year interval is incorrect.
Mr. Daves states that he used CPI-U numbers from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics for
the years 2014-2018 and calculated an inflation increase of 7.71 percent. Id. at 7-8.
Mr. Daves states that 9 of the 18 cost elements increased in excess of the 7.71
percent CPI-U inflation rate and have not been thoroughly explained by EAL as
required.
He lists the cost elements that increased more than 7.71 percent to include
Property Taxes, Miscellaneous Site Services,
Decontamination, Spent Fuel Pool
Isolation, Packaging, Removal, Ins.
& Reg. Fees, Miscellaneous Equipment, and
Characterization and Licensing Surveys for a total of $45.8 million. Id. at 10-11.
Mr. Daves states that he is concerned by the significant cost increase requested
and the 17.7 percent contingency in the 2019 Estimate.
He points out that the 2019
Estimate
does not include future
savings from technology improvements and
efficiencies that he believes are likely to occur. Id. at 11-12.
Mr. Daves provides the following recommendations:
l.
Disallow all unexplained increases for each of the cost elements that are
above the average annual inflation rate of 7.71 percent, totaling $45.8
million;
2.
In furtherance of Order No. 61 Directive 5, require EAL to address how
and to what extent it considered (i) the recent industry press reflecting
stabilized cost estimates since 2014, (2) a reduction in decommissioning
cost estimates of 2.5 percent in 2017, and (3) a ten percent lower than
anticipated cost for decommissioning Duke Energy's Crystal Creek unit;
3.
Expand Order No. 61 Directive 5 by requiring that EAL specifically address
improved efficiencies, new information and learnings, new dismantling
providers, and other technology and market developments in conjunction
with increased demand for dismantling nationwide;

Continue Order No. 61 Directive 3 by requiring EAL to file copies of any
and all reports or other filings that are made with any agency or regulatory

ANO by EAL or any other person or entity, including EAL's affiliates,

Continue Order No. 61 Directive 4 by requiring in subsequent five-year

To clarify Order No. 61 Directive 4, specify that the historical CPI-U

information
concerning
nuclear
power

that
have

operations and are in the process of decommissioning in order to
benchmark the reasonableness of its site-specific cost estimate.
The
benchmarks should include at a minimum comparisons to the actual costs
to decommission other nuclear power facilities in the United States.
In
addition, EAL should provide an updated account of any benchmarks that
are
affected by changes
in the industry,
economy,
or
regulatory

Require EAL to file its next nuclear decommissioning cost estimate by

Require EAL to continue to comply with all requirements previously

C.
EAL's Rebuttal Testimonv
EAL witness Francis Seymore states that he is a manager with TLG Services, Inc.
and is adopting the Dlrect Testimony of his colleague Mr. Cloutier, who retired in June
2019. Mr. Seymore responds to several of Staffs recommendations. Seymore Direct at
2-4.
Mr. Seymore states that Mr. Cloutier incorrectly used the CPI index for "Urban
Wage Earners and Clerical Workers" rather than the required CPI index for All Urban
APSC FILED Time: 10/9/2019 10:29:55 AM: Recvd 10/9/2019 10:29:50 AM: Docket 87-166-TF-Doc. 335

Docket No. 87-l66-TF

Consumers." He testifies that by using the wrong CPI index, Mr. Cloutier calculated an
average inflation rate of 14 percent. Mr. Seymore explains that he used this as his cost
threshold and provided an explanation for each cost element that exceeded 14 percent.
After making his own calculations using the CPI-U data, he agrees with Staff that the
average inflation rate is 7.71 percent, which he rounds to 8.0 percent. Id. at 4-5.
Mr. Seymore asserts that the CPI-U index is prone to be a poor predictor of
changes in decommissioning costs and is not surprised that decommissioning costs do
not track CPI-U very well.
He explains that a nuclear plant decommissioning project
involves mostly labor costs, and fairly specialized labor at that, but the CPI-U has less
than a ten percent component related to energy costs. Id. at 6.
Mr. Seymore provides explanations for the cost elements that exceeded the CPI-
U. Id. at 7-13. He states that TLG has employed the most up-to-date information on
decommissioning processes and technologies for the ANO decommissioning estimate
and that has resulted in some cost decreases, and some cost increases. He affirms that
TLG stands by the accuracy of the ANO decommissioning cost estimate, and comparing
the changes in the ANO decommissioning estimate to other plant estimates, some of
which went up, and some of which went down, is not reasonably possible given the
available timeframes for testimony here.
Mr. Seymore states that TLG's estimating
methodology incorporates improved efficiencies and new information to the extent TLG
is aware of it.
He notes that some "market developments" may not be publicized
because competitive parties do not want to be outbid in the future. Id. at 14-18.
Mr. Seymore states that EAL agrees with Staffs recommendation to discontinue
the ENTOMB estimate. He also states that EAL agrees in part to continue providing the

Commission with ANO decommissioning reports. He is concerned that Staffs request
may be too broad by requesting filings made to "any agency or regulatory body." Mr.
Seymore states further that EAL agrees to continue providing explanations for costs that
exceed the CPI-U. Id. at 18-20.
Mr. Seymore suggests that the Commission not order EAL to calculate CPI-U
increase using the same methodology Mr. Daves employed. He asserts that the overall
CPI increase can be deduced accurately by merely dividing the end-year CPI value by the
beginning period CPI value. Id. at 20-21.
Mr. Seymore states that EAL agrees with Staff to file its next decommissioning
estimate by March 31, 2024. Id. at 22.
D.
StafTs Surrebuttal Testimony
Mr. Daves testifies that Staff accepts EAL's 2019 Estimate of $1.615 billion, which
excludes spent fuel management costs.
However, he expresses three concerns with
EAL's Rebuttal Testimony: l)
EAL failed to provide a thorough explanation of any
increase greater than the average annual CPI-U inflation rate; 2) EAL's rejection of the
notion that technology improvements related to decommissioning should result in lower
costs; and 3)
EAL's lack of demonstrated consideration of publicly available
information regarding decommissioning trends in the United States. Daves Surrebuttal
at 2-14.
E.
EAL's Sur-Surrebuttal Testimony
Mr. Seymore states that EAL offers partial or full agreement to most of Mr.
Daves' recommendations. Seymore Sur-Surrebuttal at 3-21.

III.
SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT
A.
Ternis ofthe Settlement
The Settling Parties have agreed upon the following terms to resolve the issues in
this Docket:
"
EAL agreed with Mr. Daves' third recommendation regarding the
discontinuation of provlding a cost estimate evaluation under the
ENTOMB method.
"
EAL agreed with Mr. Daves' fourth recommendation regarding the
calculation used to
determine which costs increases require
thorough explanations.
"
EAL agreed with Mr. Daves' fifth recommendation to require EAL
to file its next decommissioning cost estimate by March 31, 2024,
unless EAL and Staff agree to change the due date.
"
EAL agreed with Mr. Daves' sixth recommendation to require EAL
to comply with all requirements previously established in this
docket unless expressly modified by the Commission.
"
EAL agreed with Mr. Daves' tenth recommendation to provide its
best estimate of the customer rate impacts using the most current
information available to the Company at the time of its March 31,
2024 filing.
"
Mr. Daves' first recommendation would require the Company to
demonstrate, with each five-year update, an assessment of the
changing
nuclear
decommissioning
landscape,
including
technology, efficiency and market changes, and to specifically
demonstrate how such changes and advancements have informed
EAL's process and been comprehended in its decommissioning cost
study analysis. The Company agreed to discuss the more significant
changes
that
affect the
estimates
in
the
five-year updates,
understanding that the Staff is always free to examine the report
and any supporting documents it requests, and then ask specific
questions about other elements of the ANO decommissioning cost
estimates in discovery.
EAL will also discuss the reasons for
changes in specific decommissioning cost categories where changes
in those categories exceed the change in the CPI-U, which should
cover all the material changes.
"
Mr. Daves' second recommendation would require the Company to
continue the Order No. 61 directive by requiring EAL to file copies
of any and all reports or other filings that are made with the NRC to
decommission ANO, the decommissioning cost estimate for ANO
units l and 2, the decommissioning trust funds for ANO units i and

Company does
not believe that further

In regards to Mr. Daves' seventh and ninth recommendations, the

B.
Settlenient^Testimony
i. EAL Witness Seyinore
EAL wltness Seymore discusses the Settlement Agreement reached by EAL and
Staff.
He states that EAL agreed with five of Mr. Daves' recommendations, partially
agreed with four of them, and initially recommended against two of them. However, he
states that, after discussions with Staff regarding the latter two recommendations, EAL
has agreed to provide additional information in future decommissioning reports.
Seymore Settlement at 3-4.
2. StaffWitness Daves
Staff witness Daves testifies that he was an active participant in the development
of the Settlement Agreement.
He states that Staff supports the Agreement because it
reasonably addresses the additional informational needs Staff identified in its review of
the 2019 Estimate. Further, the terms of the Agreement specify additional information
to be provided in EAL's next five-year cost filing, which should provide additional
support
for
EAL's
request,
aid
Staffs
review,
and
add
transparency to
the
decommissioning cost estimation process. Daves Settlement at 2-3.
IV.
FINDINGS AND RULINGS
Based upon the totality of the evidence presented in this Docket, the Commission
finds that the Settlement Agreement is just and reasonable and in the public interest.
The Commission therefore approves EAL's updated five-year estimate of the costs of
eventual decommissioning of ANO Units i and 2 as filed on March 29, 2019.
The
Commission finds that it is reasonable for EAL to discontinue the evaluation of the

ENTOMB alternative in filings beginning in 2024. Accordingly, the Commission hereby
orders and directs as follows:
i.
EAL's 2019 cost estimate of $1.615 billion, excluding post-shutdown spent
fuel management costs, is approved for use in EAI's Rider NDCR filings in years 2019
through at least 2024;
2.
RA.L shall file its next decommissioning cost estimate by March 31, 2024,
unless EAL and Staff agree to change the due date;
3.
EAL shall discontinue the evaluation of the ENTOMB alternative in filings
beginning in 2024; and
4.
EAL shall otherwise comply with all provisions of the Settlement
Agreement.
